SEVILLE, Spain, Oct 17 : Barcelona's LaLiga juggernaut rolled into Seville on Saturday and left with the scoreboard smoking, as the leaders beat Real Betis 5-2 to make it nine wins from nine and stretch their blistering league tally to 39 goals. Lamine Yamal lit the fuse with a dazzling opener before Rodri, Gabriel Jesus, Eric Garcia and substitute Dani Olmo joined the party, while Valentin Gomez and Ez Abde replied for Betis, who played much of the second half with 10 men after Facundo Bernal was sent off for headbutting Lamine. Barca moved to 27 points, five above Atletico who won 1-0 at Espanyol, while third-placed Betis have 19 and Real Madrid sit fourth on 18 before welcoming Sevilla on Sunday, Betis manager Manuel Pellegrini made eight changes from the side that beat Porto 3-2 in the Champions League, resting several key players including Antony, Marc Bartra, Natan and Isco with a midweek European meeting against Feyenoord in mind.

Yet the hosts still made Barca sweat before the visitors eventually found space, rhythm and, after Betis were reduced to 10 men, plenty of room to turn the match into another attacking exhibition. Lamine opened the scoring in the 10th minute in familiar style, gliding in from the right before whipping a left-footed strike from the edge of the box into the top corner. Betis levelled in the 27th when Pablo Fornals collected a rebound on the right and clipped a cross into the middle for Gomez, who rose highest to head past goalkeeper Joan Garcia. Barcelona reclaimed the lead in the 41st minute when Spain captain Rodri powered in a header from Fermin Lopez's corner. Betis thought they had equalised three minutes later through Gio Lo Celso's spectacular swivelling volley from outside the box, but the effort was ruled out after Cucho Hernandez was adjudged to have handled earlier in the build-up. Jesus, signed from Arsenal in the close season, had a goal disallowed for offside shortly after the break but was not kept waiting long. In the 51st, Lamine darted down the right and squared for the Brazilian to finish neatly inside the area. A minute later Abde pulled one back on the counter, sliding a low shot inside the right post, but Betis' celebrations turned sour when Bernal was shown a straight red card following a scuffle. Lamine was booked for his part in the altercation. Barcelona made it 4-2 in the 63rd minute when Alvaro Valles failed to deal with Lamine's free kick and Pau Cubarsi headed the loose ball back across goal for Garcia to tap in. Olmo completed the rout in the 81st minute, curling a right-footed shot into the top corner from outside the box. Atletico won 1-0 at Espanyol, with Baena coming off the bench to deliver the late sting in a cagey match in Barcelona. Both sides struck the post in a tight tactical contest before Atletico's substitutes combined in the 89th, Julian Alvarez bursting down the left and squaring for Baena, who drove a fierce strike into the top corner from the edge of the box.

Source: Reuters

Police and protesters clash in some of France's worst unrest in years

The protests in France began last month at high schools in Paris' poor northern suburbs, where anger over teacher shortages and shabby facilities evolved into a broader movement focused on inequality, public spending and living standards.

French riot police run amid clashes with protesters in Paris as part of nationwide protests against the cost of living and rising fuel prices called by the "Yellow Vests" movement, joined by French high school and university students, teachers and parents demanding better school conditions and government action, as well as labour unions, workers, farmers and retirees. PARIS: Violent clashes erupted between police and protesters across France on Saturday (Oct 17), as hundreds of thousands of people protested against rising costs and declining public services in some of the country's most destructive unrest in years. The Interior Ministry said at least 272 people had been arrested after violent incidents involving hooded individuals, including in Paris, Marseille in the south, Toulouse in the southwest, Angers in the west and Lyon in east-central France. Belgium, Portugal and Italy also faced smaller-scale protests on Saturday as living costs rise in Europe, while protesters in Albania again rallied against perceived government corruption, a lack of jobs and poor education standards. French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said the government would not be "intimidated" by violence, and blamed the unrest on the "far-left" and criminals just months before a presidential election next year.

"To those who clearly want to use this violence as a 'warm-up' before the presidential election, I say clearly: We will not let ourselves be intimidated. No one will impose their political agenda through violence," he wrote in a post on X. The CGT union told Agence France-Presse news agency that 800,000 people across France had taken part in Saturday's protests. The Interior Ministry did not give an estimate, and the CGT did not respond to a Reuters request for comment. Protesters said most people had marched peacefully , and put much of the violence down to troublemakers who had set out to cause damage and clash with the police. "We are fighting because the cost of living is too harsh, because the price of fuel is too high, because high school pupils are being violently attacked and hurt all over the country just for trying to protest and ask for more teachers and decent learning conditions," said Lola, a 19-year-old protester in Paris.

TEAR GAS, FIRE AND LOOTING In some parts of Paris, police occasionally fired tear gas rounds as they retreated in the face of mostly young protesters, many of whom were dressed in black and wore hoodies, masks and goggles to protect against tear gas. By late afternoon, protesters reached prominent landmarks in central Paris, including the Champs-Elysees, Concorde and La Madeleine, which had been excluded from the authorised demonstration. On Saturday evening, as the protests wound down, protesters set ablaze objects including at least one car. Some tourists at a fashionable department store near the Paris opera were seen spluttering when they were caught in clouds of tear gas, and shops nearby were hastily shuttered. Windows of many shops and restaurants in the capital were smashed, and cars and trash cans were set on fire. In Lyon, protesters torched the tourist office. In Marseille, the mayor said the town hall had been vandalised and that additional police were being sent to the city following talks with the government. In protests partly inspired by those in France, several hundred mostly young people protested in Brussels, and some clashed with police. Belgian student groups have said they are protesting against rising education costs and reforms they fear will make higher education less accessible. In Albania , police fired what appeared to be rubber bullets at protesters during a fifth day of mass student demonstrations calling for Prime Minister Edi Rama to step down.

A Centaure, a multi-purpose intervention armoured vehicle of the French Gendarmerie Nationale, is seen in street amid clashes between protesters and the French riot police during a demonstration against the cost of living and rising fuel prices in Marseille, as part of nationwide protests called by the "Yellow Vests" movement, joined by French high school and university students, teachers and parents demanding better school conditions and government action, as well as labour unions, workers, farmers and retirees. Oct 17, 2026. (Photo: REUTERS/Manon Cruz)

In Portugal, tens of thousands took to the streets of Lisbon following days of unrest to protest against housing and other living costs. Housing prices in Portugal have doubled since 2017, fuelling one of the worst affordability crises in Europe. In Italy, a march against high costs of living in Milan degenerated into disorder, with police clearing the central Cathedral square with tear gas. Police in Bologna used water cannon to try to disperse crowds and made seven arrests after another protest turned violent, the ANSA news agency reported. FRENCH POLICE RESPONSE UNDER SCRUTINY The protests in France began last month at high schools in Paris' poor northern suburbs, where anger over teacher shortages and shabby facilities evolved into a broader movement focused on inequality, public spending and living standards. In Paris on Saturday, protesters in high-visibility vests blocked streets, recalling the Yellow Vest movement that marked President Emmanuel Macron's previous term in office. Macron, who urged calm on Friday, is entering the final stretch of his presidency, facing a fragmented political landscape and growing pressure over the economy. France's efforts to reduce public debt have failed to reassure investors, pushing government borrowing costs to their highest levels in over two decades. Police tactics have drawn criticism following injuries among demonstrators, including a teenager who lost a hand after picking up a stun grenade. Lecornu said more than 900 police officers had also been injured in previous protests. The police watchdog is investigating at least two dozen allegations of police violence.

Source: Reuters/fs

MANCHESTER, England, Oct 17 : Manchester City maintained their perfect Premier League start with a 3-2 win over Ipswich Town on Saturday, but the sight of a badly limping Erling Haaland heading straight down the tunnel added another concern to those already hanging over the club. City are appealing a ruling that they breached 114 Premier League financial rules and deny wrongdoing, but the uncertainty off the pitch has done little to disrupt them on it. Enzo Maresca's side have won seven league games from seven for their best-ever start to a Premier League season. Maresca became the first manager to win his opening seven Premier League games in charge as City bounced back from Wednesday's Champions League defeat by Paris St Germain, his first meaningful loss as City boss. Haaland struck twice after Phil Foden's first goal of the season had been cancelled out by Daizen Maeda, with the Norwegian's second his 100th non-penalty Premier League goal, reached in a record 139 appearances.

He was denied a hat-trick by an offside in the build-up before Zian Flemming's stoppage-time penalty made the scoreline closer than the game felt. But victory came at a potentially heavy cost during a punishing stretch of four games in 10 days. While Maresca had made six changes to his team from Wednesday, Mateo Kovacic, Matheus Nunes and Nico O'Reilly all went off injured, while Antoine Semenyo was also limping badly at the final whistle. "Unfortunately, in 10 minutes, we had four, five players (hurt)," Maresca said. "I don't have any news at the moment." Haaland made a beeline for the tunnel rather than staying to applaud supporters, unusual for the striker, with Semenyo hobbling off not far behind. DEFIANT VOICE "I don't know (Haaland's injury)," Maresca said. "I asked him. He said that he was okay. So hopefully, it's nothing serious." The uncertainty surrounding City has hardly dampened the mood among their supporters, who were in defiant voice at the Etihad as a stadium-record 60,817 watched the game. They loudly booed the Premier League anthem before kick-off and waved inflatable bananas, reviving a City tradition dating from their days outside the top flight in the 1980s. Supporters turned the prospect of possible relegation as a sanction into gallows humour, chanting "You're going down with the City!" at the travelling Ipswich fans. Outside the stadium, vendors did brisk business selling bananas and T-shirts carrying anti-charge slogans, including "Stick your charges where the sun don't shine" and "City til I die." "The environment was very good," Maresca said. "They just said to me that today was a record attendance, so that's also a nice thing. The fans, the club, the players, we are all together in this journey, and this is the best feeling for everyone." Maresca has said several times since the team reconvened after the international break that he has instructed his players to shut out external criticism as the club appeals the guilty verdict. Captain Ruben Dias said earlier in the week that "it's almost impossible to avoid seeing something, even us being as private as we can be and just doing our own lives on your phone. It's impossible to avoid everything." Maresca praised his players for their focus. "The players, they need to be worried about people inside the club and about me for the credit I give to them, and they are not worried about people that can judge them from outside. "But inside, I promise you that the players they are happy. The club gives credit to the players. I give credit to the players. So this is for us the most important thing." Asked about managing against City with everything that has happened off the pitch, Ipswich boss Gary O'Neil shrugged and said: "No. Just us against City trying to win. Bananas, no bananas, makes no difference."

Source: Reuters

LONDON, Oct 17 : Liverpool bounced back from last week’s 3-0 Premier League drubbing by Manchester City with a workmanlike 2-1 win at Brentford on Saturday, as winger Bradley Barcola showcased the full range of his talents despite spurning two gilt-edged chances. Keane Lewis-Potter had given the home side the lead in the 44th minute but Yehor Yarmoliuk was sent off for an attempted headbutt deep into first-half stoppage time, and Victor Munoz and Alexander Isak completed Liverpool's comeback with second-half goals to seal the three points.  "Super-happy with the win. It's a tough ground, it's a tough team to play, especially away from home. We knew it was going to be a bit of a scrappy game and it's important to come out on top," Isak said.  Vitaly Janelt picked up a second yellow card in stoppage time to leave Brentford with nine men, and Barcola then squandered another opportunity when he opted to pass rather than shoot after Liverpool broke forward on the counter-attack.

Perhaps his mind was still on his first-half opportunity, when he intercepted Janelt’s attempted header and raced clear, only to lift his effort over the onrushing goalkeeper and wide. Either way, the two chances gave Liverpool fans a glimpse of what may be to come once he settles fully on Merseyside. Signed from Paris St Germain in a deal worth up to 123 million pounds, the 24-year-old was a constant threat from his starting position on the left wing, cutting inside onto his right foot to shoot or cross and moving infield or up front whenever the opportunity arose. With opponents often deploying five players across the back against the leading sides, Barcola’s skill, agility and trickery offer Liverpool another means of unlocking compact defences following Mohamed Salah’s departure at the end of last season. "I think there's still lots to improve. We're taking steps and we're grabbing points on the way which is important. It's a tough place to come, so three points is really good," Isak said.

LIVERPOOL, Oct 17 : Chelsea goalkeeper Emi Martinez suffered a concussion after his collision with Everton's Jarrad Branthwaite and was taken to hospital for "precautionary tests", manager Xabi Alonso said after their 2-0 Premier League victory. Pedro Neto's double at the Hill Dickinson Stadium ended Everton's unbeaten start to the league season but Chelsea's victory was overshadowed by the lengthy injury stoppage in the second half. Martinez and Branthwaite came together when Everton's Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall whipped a free kick into the box and although the defender was back on his feet after treatment, the Argentina goalkeeper required treatment from paramedics. The 34-year-old was eventually strapped to a stretcher and carried off the field before being taken to hospital.

"It was a concussion but beyond that I don't know. I have only seen one clip of the incident, so we need to wait," Alonso said. "What we know is that he left the stadium conscious and right now he is in hospital doing precautionary tests. We need to wait. Hopefully it won't be too bad but we need to wait." Martinez's injury forced Alonso to give Mike Penders his Premier League debut and the 21-year-old keeper helped Chelsea keep their first clean sheet in the league since January. Penders, a Belgian youth international, may have to step in for the short term due to concussion protocols preventing Martinez returning to training immediately. Chelsea host Tottenham Hotspur in the league next Saturday followed by a League Cup fourth round game at Liverpool on October 28 and a home Premier League match against Manchester United three days later. "Mike has personality. He's brave and we have full trust with him. He did well," Alonso added. "He played in the cup games and whenever he's needed, like the other players whenever they are needed they can perform. "It's all about the squad, that all the players feel important and can have their moment whenever they are needed, and that's very positive."

MUNICH, Germany, Oct 17 : Bayern Munich obliterated RB Leipzig 6-1 on Saturday with a scintillating performance, to live up to coach Vincent Kompany's prediction before the game that his team was close to hitting top form. Kompany had said on Friday his team's consecutive draws in the league and Europe were not representative of Bayern's current level and his players proved him right, delivering a statement win, with Luis Diaz hitting a hat-trick, to silence critics. The Bavarians had drawn 2-2 against Augsburg while also conceding the fastest goal in Bundesliga history last week before a shock 3-3 draw at outsiders Viking in the Champions League on Tuesday.  They had to come from behind in both those matches but against Leipzig it was clear from the start who was boss.

Leipzig scored a late consolation goal in stoppage time. LONDON, Oct 17 : Manchester City bounced back from their midweek setback in Europe to maintain their perfect Premier League start with Erling Haaland's double propelling them to a 3-2 home win over battling Ipswich Town on Saturday. Paris St Germain inflicted a first meaningful defeat on Enzo Maresca's side in the Champions League on Wednesday but City shrugged off a gallant Ipswich side to make it seven wins from seven to cement their place at the top of the table. Chelsea beat Everton 2-0 in Saturday's early action thanks to Pedro Neto's brace although the London club's win was overshadowed by an injury to goalkeeper Emi Martinez. Liverpool came from a goal down to beat Brentford 2-1 away although they were helped by the previously unbeaten hosts being reduced to 10 men shortly before halftime when Yehor Yarmolyuk was shown a straight red card for a head butt.

Manchester City have 21 points, six ahead of second-placed champions Arsenal, who visit Nottingham Forest on Sunday. Liverpool's win lifted them above Brentford into fifth place with 12 points behind Chelsea in fourth on 13. Third-placed Brighton & Hove Albion, who also have 13 points, host Crystal Palace on Sunday. Fulham moved off the foot of the table with their first league win of the season - 1-0 at home to Hull City - while Aston Villa won by the same scoreline at Newcastle United. BUSINESS AS USUAL FOR CITY Dark clouds remain over the Etihad Stadium with Manchester City's fate still unknown after they appealed a ruling that the club breached 114 Premier League financial rules. City have always denied any wrongdoing. But on the pitch it is very much business as usual, especially for Norwegian goal machine Haaland. Phil Foden gave City a short-lived lead cancelled out by Daizen Maeda, but Haaland restored the home side's advantage before halftime with a header from Mateo Kovacic's cross. Haaland then gave his side some breathing space with his second in the 69th minute, powering past Ipswich's Abdoul Ouattara before a low finish into the corner. He was denied a hat-trick by an offside decision and Ipswich got a lifeline when Zian Flemming tucked away a penalty in stoppage time but City bagged the points. The defiant mood was soured somewhat though as Haaland went off with an apparent injury late on, as did Mateo Kovacic, Matheus Nunes and Nico O'Reilly, while Antoine Semenyo was also limping badly at the final whistle. "I don't know (Haaland's injury)," Maresca said. "I asked him. He said that he was okay. So hopefully, it's nothing serious." FEISTY FIRST HALF Chelsea have had a knack of scoring early this season but were kept at bay by hosts Everton in a feisty and physical first half that produced five yellow cards. However, Xabi Alonso's visitors needed just 43 seconds after the restart to go 1-0 up when Jorrel Hato cut the ball back from the byline to find Neto who swept home. Keeper Martinez's clash of heads with Jarrad Branthwaite resulted in the Argentine being strapped to a stretcher and taken off, leading to 11 minutes of stoppage time. Chelsea doubled their lead in the 90th minute when Neto pounced on a loose ball after Jordan Henderson's free kick was blocked by the wall, finding the bottom corner with a composed finish as Everton suffered their first defeat of the season. "What we know is he (Martinez) left the stadium conscious and right now he is in the hospital doing precautionary tests," Alonso said. "It was concussion but more than that I saw only one clip. Hopefully it won't be too bad but we need to wait." Martinez's knock gave 21-year-old keeper Mike Penders the chance to make his Premier League debut and he helped Chelsea keep a clean sheet in the league for the first time in 23 games. "We need a clean sheet, to be honest. I think we did a very good game. Emi deserved this, Mike did as well," Alonso added. BRENTFORD'S YARMOLYUK SENT OFF Liverpool deservedly fell behind at Brentford with Keane Lewis-Potter putting the hosts in front. Brentford were good value for their lead but Yarmolyuk's rush of blood to the head when he clashed with Jeremy Jacquet at a Liverpool corner changed the game. After referee John Brooks was invited to check a VAR monitor he brandished the red card at Ukrainian Yarmolyuk. Liverpool huffed and puffed after the break but Victor Munoz finally levelled in the 62nd minute when he cut in to beat keeper Caoimhin Kelleher with a left-foot finish. Alexander Isak won it for Andoni Iraola's side eight minutes later with a clinical strike from Bradley Barcola's assist. Brentford ended with nine men after Vitaly Janelt got a second yellow card for a foul on substitute Rio Ngumoha. Alex Iwobi's 33rd-minute strike for Fulham was enough to earn their new manager Alvaro Arbeloa a long-overdue league win and move Fulham up to 16th. Johan Manzambi's early goal secured Villa's victory at Newcastle, their second of the season.

NEW DELHI: India's "cockroach" youth movement leader was released by an Indian court on Saturday (Oct 17), a day after he was detained for trying to lead another protest rally in New Delhi calling for the resignation of the country's election chief. Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), rose to prominence this year when a weeks-long sit-in contributed to India's education minister resigning. CJP's legal affairs head Ratna Singh said Dipke was released after he agreed to certain conditions. Singh gave no details of the terms. Dipke's youth-led group, opposition parties and student organisations have held near-daily protests this month demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over a revision of voter lists that they say favours Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).

More than 130 million voters were deleted during the revision. The Election Commission has denied favouring any party and said wrongly deleted voters can re-enrol. The BJP has accused rivals of trying to undermine democracy by wrongly questioning legitimate electoral processes. Student activist Neha Bora, a prominent face of the protests, who was also detained on Friday as she tried to reach central Delhi with dozens of supporters, was released on Saturday. "Please, spare the people of India. Impeach Gyanesh Kumar and halt SIR (special intensive revision), so that the ordinary citizens of this country can breathe a sigh of relief, feel at ease, and have their voting rights ensured," Bora told ANI news agency after she was released.

STUDENT GROUPS CALL FOR MORE PROTEST ACTION Dipke was detained on Friday as he stepped out of a house in central Delhi, with police hauling him into a police car and driving away after a brief argument. Dipke had called Friday's protest in support of two CJP leaders detained and sent to jail this week for five days for demonstrating at a protest site in violation of a ban. Earlier on Friday, police had met Dipke and warned him against going ahead with the protest. Student groups called for more protest action on Saturday. The movement, which was mobilised by the youth and joined by many opposition parties, has emerged as one of the biggest political challenges faced by Modi and the BJP in the prime minister's 12 years in power.

FAST

BANGKOK, Oct 17 : Rapidly improving artificial intelligence capabilities will bring far faster change across all fields, Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark said on Saturday, with one of the company's internal models forecasting that under certain conditions it could increase US economic output by almost 50 per cent by 2030. Clark, speaking at IMF and World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok, said that international cooperation was needed to erect "unusual and serious rules" for the transformative technology, and there was a shrinking window for policymakers to act. Clark said that the estimated potential US GDP of $44 trillion, which compares to the current level of just over $30 trillion, "sounds very outlandish, I know." But he added that AI was vastly increasing scientific discovery. He said the forecast assumed "the technology continuing to get better. And if GDP were to grow this much, then economic doctrine suggests that new industries and inventions would need to have been created to power such a major economic expansion".

Clark's remarks come as the company prepares for an initial public offering expected in November that could value the firm at up to $2 trillion.  HUMANS IN CONTROL, FOR NOW Clark issued a wake-up call to policymakers about the speed of AI development, saying there was growing evidence of a "singularity" where AI development outpaces human control. "We should expect that in the coming years, the whole pace of progress of not just AI but science as a whole will speed up, and this will feel confusing and disorienting, and will bring with it great wealth and potentially great peril," he said in a lecture to hundreds of government and finance officials. AI was a major topic at the IMF and World Bank meetings, as both a source of growth offsetting high energy prices and a potential threat to stability if it falls short of its promise as a productivity game-changer and stock valuations crash.  Officials also expressed worries about AI destroying certain jobs and leaving some countries behind. But Clark, a former journalist who serves as Anthropic's "head of public benefit," painted a picture of a rosy future where AI was a force multiplier for scientific discovery, solving mathematical, engineering and biological problems, including new drug discovery, as human researchers are supplemented by hundreds or thousands of AI assistants.  More countries can participate in the AI revolution by helping to build the data center computing capacity needed to power AI, he said. STRICTEST CONTROLS ON BIOLOGICAL RESEARCH Clark cautioned that global leaders need to understand how powerful AI will become and make urgent choices about how to regulate the technology. "Being able to use AI for science opens us up to the misuses of science as well, biological and cyber weapons and things we cannot yet imagine, and we have many choices to make," he said. Biological research, where AI has already created new viruses, is an area "where we want the strictest human oversight and transparency to maintain safety." Despite some recent high-profile incidents where rogue AI systems have escaped testing environments and hacked websites and databases, he said AI was still under human control. But the window to impose safeguards was shrinking as AI became more capable and was now "a small number of years."  Clark also acknowledged that AI was causing job losses in some fields with "high AI exposure" such as call centers and customer service personnel. But for other fields, such as scientific research, he said AI was enhancing employment and a major unknown was its potential to create jobs in completely new industries.

Source: Reuters

"We're well aware you can put yourself under pressure the way that we're trying to play, but we'll also back ourselves that we'll profit more than we'll suffer in those situations.  "I don't think you want all the teams in the world playing the same game. I think if you look at the Wallabies, they're pretty similar to us. I think they'll want to play, and it's a point of difference, part of the DNA of both sides."  "If you want to just get into arm wrestles with a couple of the big sides in the world, it'll be a struggle," he said.   Despite his team scoring six tries with some breathtaking rugby in the first half on Saturday, Rennie said there were still improvements to be made.  "We're trying to grow our game, and we've got a long way to go," he said.  "We just want to be able to play at a tempo that will test other sides."  Australia coach Les Kiss said he was pleased with the performance of flyhalf Declan Meredith in only his fourth test and remained confident the Wallabies could put on a good showing at their home World Cup next year.    "I've always said we'll have ups and downs, and today it was a bit of a downer again," he said.  "But there are some good clues about what we're trying to do in our game. When we do play with footy in the hand with a positive intent, we're making a lot of breaks against one of the best teams in the world.  "So I think there are some good qualities that are coming through. So I'm optimistic still."

Source: Reuters

SYDNEY, Oct 17 : The All Blacks rode a first-half try blitz to a 43-21 victory over the Wallabies at Stadium Australia on Saturday, extending their win streak over their trans-Tasman-Sea rivals to 13 matches.  With the Bledisloe Cup already safely in the cupboard for a 24th year after last week's 50-19 win in Auckland, New Zealand exploded out of the blocks and crushed all thoughts of an upset with six tries before the break.  Despite losing Jordie Barrett to a calf injury before kickoff and another centre in Quinn Tupaea early on with a concussion, the All Blacks overwhelmed the Wallabies with power, pace and precision in the opening 40 minutes. "I'm really proud of the boys, the way we came out on that in that first half," said New Zealand captain Codie Taylor.

"It was a real challenge for us this week to make sure that we backed up a really good performance from last week, and I thought we were awesome in that first 40." Australia showed some flashes of backline brilliance, particularly in the second half, but struggled to get hold of the ball for prolonged periods and were unable to match the accuracy or clinical finishing of the All Blacks.    In a whirlwind of offloads, winger Josh Moorby, fullback Beauden Barrett, flanker Peter Lakai and replacement back Rieko Ioane all crossed in the first 26 minutes to give the visitors a quick-fire 22-0 lead.  Wallabies flyhalf Declan Meredith did well to get a pass away in the tackle just before the half-hour mark to send Jeremy Williams over for a try but the lock was sin-binned at the other end of the field two minutes later.  All Blacks number eight Wallace Sititi immediately made the extra man count with his team's fifth try and Beauden Barrett added a sixth, his second, off an intercept to send New Zealand into the break with a 36-7 lead. Moorby faked out the defence for his second five-pointer within three minutes of the restart before the Wallabies finally finished off a backline move for fullback Tom Wright to go over.  Australia were looking stronger with their replacements on the pitch, and Meredith almost scored a try after a scything break up the middle, then saved a try at the other end. A clever line dropout from Wright did result in a third Australia try in the 66th minute for replacement back Filipo Daugunu that delighted the majority of the crowd of 73,399.    New Zealand were reduced to 14 men after Samisoni Taukei'aho went off injured, and went down to 13 when debutant Chay Fihaki was shown a yellow card but managed to hold out the Wallabies for the last few minutes. "I'm gutted," said Wallabies captain Harry Wilson. "When you give a team like the All Blacks a head start it's tough, and it's not good enough for this group. "We've got to be a lot better. It's been a very disappointing series, and we're going to have to regroup."

Source: Reuters
